tasks_completed.description: Extended TrackedSession interface with respawn metadata fields
tasks_completed.changes: Added workingDirectory, claudeSessionId, stoppingByDaemon, respawnCount, lastCrashAt fields to TrackedSession
tasks_completed.rationale: Daemon needs working directory and Claude session ID to respawn crashed sessions, stoppingByDaemon flag to distinguish daemon-initiated SIGTERM from crashes, and respawnCount/lastCrashAt for backoff

tasks_completed.description: Implemented event-driven respawn logic in daemon onChildExited
changes: onChildExited now receives exitCode and signal parameters
happyProcess.on('exit') handler passes code and signal to onChildExited
happyProcess.on('error') handler passes exit code 1 to onChildExited
onChildExited inspects exit code: 0 or null = clean exit (no respawn), non-zero = crash (respawn)
stoppingByDaemon flag checked to prevent respawning daemon-stopped sessions
Respawn requires claudeSessionId AND workingDirectory to be present
stopSession() sets stoppingByDaemon=true before SIGTERM for both daemon-spawned and external sessions
workingDirectory stored in TrackedSession on spawn (from options.directory)
claudeSessionId and workingDirectory stored from metadata webhook
tasks_completed.rationale: Root cause: count-based watcher cannot distinguish crash from archive. Solution: daemon has exit code information and can make correct respawn decisions per-session

tasks_completed.description: Removed watcher auto-restore trigger from watch_sessions()
tasks_completed.changes: Removed the 'if [ $nr -gt 0 ]; then restore_online_sessions & fi' block from watch_sessions(). Watcher now only records state changes and maintains snapshots.
tasks_completed.rationale: The watcher's count-based auto-restore was the root cause of cascade bugs (Bug #62). With daemon-level respawn, the watcher is now a passive observer.

tasks_completed.changes: Removed 'break' statement that stopped search after first home. Added SCOPE_HOME support to limit search when scoped.
tasks_completed.rationale: Bug caused peak snapshot search to only check /root/.happy, missing jade/dev/qijie snapshots

tasks_completed.description: Fixed read_snapshot_count to aggregate across homes
tasks_completed.changes: When SCOPE_HOME is set, reads only that home's count. In global mode, sums counts across all homes instead of returning first home's count.
tasks_completed.rationale: Previous behavior only returned first home's count, causing incorrect peak protection calculations for multi-daemon setups

tasks_completed.changes: Default daemon now emits explicit '/root/.happy' as home_dir instead of empty string. Both Source 1 (PID lookup) and Source 2 (daemon /list) now use home_dir_val='$home' for all daemons.
tasks_completed.rationale: Empty string for default daemon caused filter_sessions_for_home to misidentify sessions, especially with qijie daemon added

changes: Without flag: only spawns missing sessions, skips already-running ones
With flag: kills orphans first, then spawns all (used by ExecStartPost)
happy-daemon-post-start.sh now passes --kill-orphans to restore command
restore) case handler parses both --home and --kill-orphans arguments
tasks_completed.rationale: ExecStartPost needs to kill orphans from previous daemon instance before respawning. Normal restore (e.g. from restart_daemon) should not kill running sessions.

git_rationale.root_cause_commit: N/A - architectural design flaw, not a single commit
git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: The watcher used count-based heuristics to detect disappeared sessions and trigger auto-restore. Count drops cannot distinguish between crash (should restore) and archive (should NOT restore).
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: Moved single-session crash recovery to the daemon's onChildExited handler which has direct access to exit codes. Exit code 0 = clean exit (archive, natural completion) = no respawn. Non-zero exit code (1, 137=OOM, 143=SIGTERM) with no stoppingByDaemon flag = crash = respawn. The watcher is now a passive observer that only maintains snapshots for ExecStartPost recovery.

dev.qa_notes: Verification checks passed: bash -n for both scripts, npx tsc --noEmit for TypeScript. Key areas to test: (1) Archive a session and verify daemon does NOT respawn it. (2) Verify watcher logs count changes but never triggers restore. (3) Verify ExecStartPost restore still works with --kill-orphans. (4) Verify find_peak_snapshot searches all homes. TDD skipped: daemon process lifecycle is not programmatically testable without spawning real processes. The BA/PM already identified the root cause via behavioral observation.
implementation_notes: run.ts already had pre-existing quality gate violations (848 lines, 780-line function). Edits were applied via Python script to work within existing constraints. The file needs a future refactor to extract spawnSession/stopSession/onChildExited into a separate module.

filter_sessions_for_home still has a backward-compatibility fallback for empty home_dir (old snapshots). This is correct since historical JSON snapshots may contain home_dir='' for default daemon sessions.
The respawn carries over respawnCount to the newly spawned session so backoff persists across respawns. After 3 consecutive crashes, the daemon gives up.

recommendations: Refactor run.ts to extract session management functions into separate modules (spawnSession, stopSession, onChildExited) to comply with quality gate thresholds
Consider adding a /respawn-status endpoint to the daemon HTTP control server for monitoring
Old JSON snapshots with empty home_dir for default daemon should be treated as /root/.happy during migration
